# extend git at for future

Let `git at` shift into the future as well as into the past:

```bash
$ git at +4h
-> time.Now().Add(4*time.Hour)
```

The offset parser assumed a leading `-`; a `+` (or no sign) should add the duration, so that a commit can be dated later in the day when work is recorded ahead of time.
